column3: Used mostly in the north. In the south and in Taiwan the usual word for it is 外婆.
column4: 我姥姥住在北京。
column5: 我姥姥住在北京。
column6: Wǒ lǎolao zhù zài Běijīng.
column7: My grandmother lives in Beijing.
column9: Used mostly in the north. In the south and in Taiwan the usual word for it is 外婆.

column3: A warm, caring love shown by someone older or in charge toward someone dear to them, such as a parent for a child or a grandparent for a grandchild: 疼爱孙子.
column4: 奶奶很疼爱她的孙子。
column5: 奶奶很疼愛她的孫子。
column6: Nǎinai hěn téng'ài tā de sūnzi.
column7: Grandma dotes on her grandson.
column9: A warm, caring love shown by someone older or in charge toward someone dear to them, such as a parent for a child or a grandparent for a grandchild: 疼愛孫子.

column3: Besides the body part (胸口, the front of the chest), it also stands for one's heart and mind in words such as 胸怀 (bosom, outlook). It was first written 匈, with 肉 added later.
column4: 我胸口有点疼。
column5: 我胷口有點疼。
column6: Wǒ xiōng kǒu yǒu diǎn téng.
column7: My chest hurts a little.
column9: Besides the body part (胸口, the front of the chest), it also stands for one's heart and mind in words such as 胸懷 (bosom, outlook). It was first written 匈, with 肉 added later.

column3: The back of the body, as in 后背疼 (a sore back). Used for the back part of a thing too, when "behind" is meant.
column4: 我后背有点痒。
column5: 我後背有點癢。
column6: Wǒ hòubèi yǒu diǎn yǎng.
column7: My back is a little itchy.
column9: The back of the body, as in 後背疼 (a sore back). Used for the back part of a thing too, when "behind" is meant.

column3: Used both for the throat as it feels (嗓子疼, a sore throat; 嗓子哑, a hoarse voice) and for a singing voice (好嗓子).
column4: 我嗓子疼，不想说话。
column5: 我嗓子疼，不想說話。
column6: Wǒ sǎngzi téng, bù xiǎng shuōhuà.
column7: My throat hurts and I do not want to talk.
column9: Used both for the throat as it feels (嗓子疼, a sore throat; 嗓子啞, a hoarse voice) and for a singing voice (好嗓子).

column3: The measure word is 条 or 道. By itself 眉 lives on in a few words, such as 眉头 (the brow) and 皱眉 (to frown).
column4: 她的眉毛又黑又长。
column5: 她的眉毛又黑又長。
column6: Tā de méimao yòu hēi yòu cháng.
column7: Her eyebrows are dark and long.
column9: The measure word is 條 or 道. By itself 眉 lives on in a few words, such as 眉頭 (the brow) and 皺眉 (to frown).

column3: 打 is the verb for a body reflex: 打喷嚏, 打哈欠 (to yawn), 打嗝 (to hiccup). To count them, say 打了一个喷嚏.
column4: 我感冒了，一直打喷嚏。
column5: 我感冒了，一直打噴嚏。
column6: Wǒ gǎnmào le, yī zhí dǎpēntì.
column7: I have a cold and keep sneezing.
column9: 打 is the verb for a body reflex: 打噴嚏, 打哈欠 (to yawn), 打嗝 (to hiccup). To count them, say 打了一個噴嚏.

column3: It names the cause, getting chilled from a cold wind, thin clothes or an open window, and a cold (感冒) may follow: 小心着凉 is a common warning. In Taiwan the first syllable is said zhāo.
column4: 晚上很冷，小心着凉。
column5: 晚上很冷，小心著涼。
column6: Wǎnshang hěn lěng, xiǎoxīn zháoliáng.
column7: It is cold at night, so be careful not to catch a chill.
column9: It names the cause, getting chilled from a cold wind, thin clothes or an open window, and a cold (感冒) may follow: 小心著涼 is a common warning. In Taiwan the first syllable is said zhāo.

column3: Often a warning or a complaint: 别熬夜 (do not stay up late), 熬夜伤身体 (staying up hurts your health). It is a verb with its object built in, so you say 熬了一夜 for staying up all night.
column4: 他昨天熬夜写报告。
column5: 他昨天熬夜寫報告。
column6: Tā zuótiān áoyè xiě bàogào.
column7: He stayed up late yesterday writing a report.
column9: Often a warning or a complaint: 別熬夜 (do not stay up late), 熬夜傷身體 (staying up hurts your health). It is a verb with its object built in, so you say 熬了一夜 for staying up all night.

column3: 冰 translates "ice" and 激凌 imitates the sound of "cream". The same word is also written 冰淇淋, common on the mainland too and the only spelling in Taiwan.
column4: 夏天我爱吃冰激凌。
column5: 夏天我愛吃冰激凌。
column6: Xiàtiān wǒ ài chī bīngjīlíng.
column7: In summer I love eating ice cream.
column9: 冰 translates "ice" and 激凌 imitates the sound of "cream". The same word is also written 冰淇淋, common on the mainland too and the only spelling in Taiwan.

column3: A small, loose-skinned orange; the larger sweet orange is 橙子. The standard spelling is 橘子, the usual one in Taiwan; 桔子 is a common simpler spelling on the mainland.
column4: 我想吃一个桔子。
column5: 我想吃一個桔子。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng chī yī gè júzi.
column7: I want to eat a tangerine.
column9: A small, loose-skinned orange; the larger sweet orange is 橙子. The standard spelling is 橘子, the usual one in Taiwan; 桔子 is a common simpler spelling on the mainland.

column3: Mostly a modifier on food: 油炸食品 (fried foods), 油炸鸡腿 (fried drumsticks). On its own, 炸 can also mean to burst or to explode, said zhà.
column4: 油炸的食物吃多了不健康。
column5: 油炸的食物吃多了不健康。
column6: Yóuzhá de shíwù chī duō le bù jiànkāng.
column7: Eating too much fried food is not healthy.
column9: Mostly a modifier on food: 油炸食品 (fried foods), 油炸雞腿 (fried drumsticks). On its own, 炸 can also mean to burst or to explode, said zhà.

column3: Seen in 茶壶 (teapot) and 水壶 (kettle or water bottle). It is also the measure word for what a pot holds: 一壶茶. The word hú may be a contraction of 葫芦, "calabash" (one scholar's view).
column4: 我们点了一壶茶。
column5: 我們點了一壺茶。
column6: Wǒmen diǎn le yī hú chá.
column7: We ordered a pot of tea.
column9: Seen in 茶壺 (teapot) and 水壺 (kettle or water bottle). It is also the measure word for what a pot holds: 一壺茶. The word hú may be a contraction of 葫蘆, "calabash" (one scholar's view).

column3: A garage for a car, and also a parking garage in a building: 地下车库 is an underground one. An open parking lot is 停车场.
column4: 车库里停着一辆车。
column5: 車庫裡停著一輛車。
column6: Chēkù lǐ tíngzhe yī liàng chē.
column7: There is a car parked in the garage.
column9: A garage for a car, and also a parking garage in a building: 地下車庫 is an underground one. An open parking lot is 停車場.

column3: The measure word is 把. The verb is 梳, as in 梳头 (to comb one's hair); adding 子 gives the tool itself.
column4: 你有梳子吗？
column5: 你有梳子嗎？
column6: Nǐ yǒu shūzi ma?
column7: Do you have a comb?
column9: The measure word is 把. The verb is 梳, as in 梳頭 (to comb one's hair); adding 子 gives the tool itself.

column3: A catch-all for anything that pinches or grips, so the kind is often said in front: 衣服夹子 is a clothespin, and 文件夹 is a folder.
column4: 她用夹子把头发夹起来。
column5: 她用夾子把頭髮夾起來。
column6: Tā yòng jiāzi bǎ tóufa jiā qǐlái.
column7: She clips her hair up with a clip.
column9: A catch-all for anything that pinches or grips, so the kind is often said in front: 衣服夾子 is a clothespin, and 文件夾 is a folder.

column3: Any hollow tube or pipe, such as a water pipe or a hose; a drinking straw is usually 吸管. The same spelling is also the name Guǎnzǐ, a classical book, where 子 is read zǐ.
column4: 这根管子堵住了。
column5: 這根管子堵住了。
column6: Zhè gēn guǎnzi dǔ zhù le.
column7: This pipe is blocked.
column9: Any hollow tube or pipe, such as a water pipe or a hose; a drinking straw is usually 吸管. The same spelling is also the name Guǎnzǐ, a classical book, where 子 is read zǐ.

column3: It comes before a verb or noun: 随身携带 (to carry on one's person), 随身行李 (carry-on baggage), 随身听 (a portable music player).
column4: 请随身携带您的证件。
column5: 請隨身攜帶您的證件。
column6: Qǐng suíshēn xiédài nín de zhèngjiàn.
column7: Please carry your ID with you.
column9: It comes before a verb or noun: 隨身攜帶 (to carry on one's person), 隨身行李 (carry-on baggage), 隨身聽 (a portable music player).

column3: The verb is 戴, as with other jewelry: 戴项链, 戴耳环. The measure word is 条.
column4: 她戴着一条金项链。
column5: 她戴著一條金項鏈。
column6: Tā dàizhe yī tiáo jīn xiàngliàn.
column7: She is wearing a gold necklace.
column9: The verb is 戴, as with other jewelry: 戴項鏈, 戴耳環. The measure word is 條.

column3: The verb is 戴. A pair is 一对耳环 and a single one is 一只耳环; a ring for the finger is 戒指.
column4: 她今天戴了新耳环。
column5: 她今天戴了新耳環。
column6: Tā jīntiān dài le xīn ěrhuán.
column7: She is wearing new earrings today.
column9: The verb is 戴. A pair is 一對耳環 and a single one is 一隻耳環; a ring for the finger is 戒指.

column3: Here 系 is read jì, "to tie", not xì. It goes with things fastened around you: 系领带, 系鞋带 (tie shoelaces), 系安全带 (buckle a seat belt).
column4: 他每天都系领带上班。
column5: 他每天都繫領帶上班。
column6: Tā měi tiān dōu jìlǐngdài shàngbān.
column7: He wears a tie to work every day.
column9: Here 繫 means "to tie" and is read jì. It goes with things fastened around you: 繫領帶, 繫鞋帶 (tie shoelaces), 繫安全帶 (buckle a seat belt).

column3: It describes a person or a look that is up to date: 很时髦. 赶时髦 is "to follow fashion". 时尚 can also name the whole field of fashion, while 时髦 mostly describes a person or item.
column4: 她穿得很时髦。
column5: 她穿得很時髦。
column6: Tā chuān de hěn shímáo.
column7: She dresses very fashionably.
column9: It describes a person or a look that is up to date: 很時髦. 趕時髦 is "to follow fashion". 時尚 can also name the whole field of fashion, while 時髦 mostly describes a person or item.

column3: Both an adjective and a noun, and the noun names the field itself: 时尚杂志 (fashion magazine), 引领时尚 (to set the trend).
column4: 这个品牌的衣服很时尚。
column5: 這個品牌的衣服很時尚。
column6: Zhège pǐnpái de yīfu hěn shíshàng.
column7: This brand's clothes are very stylish.
column9: Both an adjective and a noun, and the noun names the field itself: 時尚雜誌 (fashion magazine), 引領時尚 (to set the trend).

column3: A loanword from English "model", for a person who models clothes or poses for photos or artists: 男模特, 女模特. A scale model of an object is 模型.
column4: 她是一名模特。
column5: 她是一名模特。
column6: Tā shì yī míng mótè.
column7: She is a model.
column9: A loanword from English "model", for a person who models clothes or poses for photos or artists: 男模特, 女模特. A scale model of an object is 模型.

column3: A compliment: slim and graceful. 瘦 means thin and need not be flattering. It is almost always said of women: 身材苗条.
column4: 她身材苗条。
column5: 她身材苗條。
column6: Tā shēncái miáotiao.
column7: She has a slender figure.
column9: A compliment: slim and graceful. 瘦 means thin and need not be flattering. It is almost always said of women: 身材苗條.

column3: The neutral or scientific word for insects, as in school books and nature programs. In casual talk people say 虫子 or name the animal, such as 蚂蚁 for an ant.
column4: 蚂蚁是一种昆虫。
column5: 螞蟻是一種昆蟲。
column6: Mǎyǐ shì yī zhǒng kūnchóng.
column7: Ants are a kind of insect.
column9: The neutral or scientific word for insects, as in school books and nature programs. In casual talk people say 蟲子 or name the animal, such as 螞蟻 for an ant.

column3: The verb is 养: 养宠物 means to keep a pet. Related places are 宠物店 (pet shop) and 宠物医院 (vet clinic).
column4: 我家有两只宠物。
column5: 我家有兩隻寵物。
column6: Wǒ jiā yǒu liǎng zhī chǒngwù.
column7: We have two pets at home.
column9: The verb is 養: 養寵物 means to keep a pet. Related places are 寵物店 (pet shop) and 寵物醫院 (vet clinic).

column3: In speech it is nearly always 彩虹 rather than 虹 alone. A bare 虹 survives in a few set words, such as 霓虹灯 (neon light).
column4: 雨后天空出现了彩虹。
column5: 雨後天空出現了彩虹。
column6: Yǔ hòu tiānkōng chūxiàn le cǎihóng.
column7: A rainbow appeared in the sky after the rain.
column9: In speech it is nearly always 彩虹 rather than 虹 alone. A bare 虹 survives in a few set words, such as 霓虹燈 (neon light).

column3: Besides thunder (打雷 is "thunder rumbles"), it is the 雷 of 地雷, a land mine, and colloquially it means to stun or shock someone, as in 被雷到.
column4: 昨天晚上打雷了，我睡不着。
column5: 昨天晚上打雷了，我睡不著。
column6: Zuótiān wǎnshang dǎ léi le, wǒ shuì bù zháo.
column7: There was thunder last night and I could not sleep.
column9: Besides thunder (打雷 is "thunder rumbles"), it is the 雷 of 地雷, a land mine, and colloquially it means to stun or shock someone, as in 被雷到.

column3: The everyday word for dust that settles on furniture or floats in the air: 擦灰尘 is to wipe it off, 满是灰尘 is covered in it. Dust from soil outdoors is more often 尘土. 灰 is a fire 火 that can be touched with the hand: what is left is ash.
column4: 桌子上有一层灰尘。
column5: 桌子上有一層灰塵。
column6: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu yī céng huīchén.
column7: There is a layer of dust on the table.
column9: The everyday word for dust that settles on furniture or floats in the air: 擦灰塵 is to wipe it off, 滿是灰塵 is covered in it. Dust from soil outdoors is more often 塵土. 灰 is a fire 火 that can be touched with the hand: what is left is ash.

column3: Said of air, weather, skin, lips and soil: 空气干燥, 皮肤干燥. It can also mean dull, as in a dry lecture. For dried food or clothes that are dry, 干 alone is the word.
column4: 冬天空气很干燥，要多喝水。
column5: 冬天空氣很乾燥，要多喝水。
column6: Dōngtiān kōngqì hěn gānzào, yào duō hē shuǐ.
column7: The air is very dry in winter, so drink more water.
column9: Said of air, weather, skin, lips and soil: 空氣乾燥, 皮膚乾燥. It can also mean dull, as in a dry lecture. For dried food or clothes that are dry, 乾 alone is the word.

column3: Pleasantly moist rather than wet: said of air, soil, skin and eyes, and used mostly in a good sense. A soaked towel is just 湿; 眼睛湿润 means eyes filling with tears.
column4: 南方的空气很湿润。
column5: 南方的空氣很濕潤。
column6: Nánfāng de kōngqì hěn shīrùn.
column7: The air in the south is very humid.
column9: Pleasantly moist rather than wet: said of air, soil, skin and eyes, and used mostly in a good sense. A soaked towel is just 溼; 眼睛濕潤 means eyes filling with tears.

column3: A somewhat formal word for islands as a group or in general, common in news and geography: 沿海岛屿, 大小岛屿. For one particular island in speech, 岛 alone is enough.
column4: 这个国家有几千个岛屿。
column5: 這個國家有幾千個島嶼。
column6: Zhège guójiā yǒu jǐ qiān gè dǎoyǔ.
column7: This country has several thousand islands.
column9: A somewhat formal word for islands as a group or in general, common in news and geography: 沿海島嶼, 大小島嶼. For one particular island in speech, 島 alone is enough.

column3: A small pond, usually still and shallow, with fish, lotus or ducks in it. A bigger body of water is a 湖, and a swimming pool is 游泳池.
column4: 池塘里有几条金鱼。
column5: 池塘裡有幾條金魚。
column6: Chítáng lǐ yǒu jǐ tiáo jīnyú.
column7: There are a few goldfish in the pond.
column9: A small pond, usually still and shallow, with fish, lotus or ducks in it. A bigger body of water is a 湖, and a swimming pool is 游泳池.

column3: Coal as a fuel and an industry: 煤炭工业, 煤炭价格, 煤炭发电. In everyday speech 煤 alone is common (烧煤), while 炭 alone usually means charcoal.
column4: 这个城市以前主要靠煤炭发电。
column5: 這個城市以前主要靠煤炭發電。
column6: Zhège chéngshì yǐqián zhǔyào kào méitàn fādiàn.
column7: This city used to rely mainly on coal for electricity.
column9: Coal as a fuel and an industry: 煤炭工業, 煤炭價格, 煤炭發電. In everyday speech 煤 alone is common (燒煤), while 炭 alone usually means charcoal.

column3: Steel as a material and an industry: 钢铁厂, 钢铁工业. It is also a figure of speech for strength and will, as in 钢铁般的意志, an iron will.
column4: 这家钢铁厂有一万多名工人。
column5: 這家鋼鐵廠有一萬多名工人。
column6: Zhè jiā gāngtiě chǎng yǒu yī wàn duō míng gōngrén.
column7: This steel plant has more than ten thousand workers.
column9: Steel as a material and an industry: 鋼鐵廠, 鋼鐵工業. It is also a figure of speech for strength and will, as in 鋼鐵般的意志, an iron will.

column3: Silk as a cloth and a product: 丝绸衬衫, 丝绸围巾, and the 丝绸之路, the Silk Road. Silk thread itself is 丝. 丝 comes from doubling 糸, the silk thread.
column4: 这条围巾是丝绸做的，摸起来很软。
column5: 這條圍巾是絲綢做的，摸起來很軟。
column6: Zhè tiáo wéijīn shì sīchóu zuò de, mō qǐlái hěn ruǎn.
column7: This scarf is made of silk and feels very soft.
column9: Silk as a cloth and a product: 絲綢襯衫, 絲綢圍巾, and the 絲綢之路, the Silk Road. Silk thread itself is 絲. 絲 comes from doubling 糸, the silk thread.

column3: A spoken word for young and soft things: 嫩叶, 嫩草, tender vegetables, meat cooked just right, baby skin. It is the opposite of 老. It can also mean a light shade of color, or inexperienced when said of a person.
column4: 这种青菜很嫩，炒一下就好了。
column5: 這種青菜很嫩，炒一下就好了。
column6: Zhè zhǒng qīngcài hěn nèn, chǎo yī xià jiù hǎo le.
column7: This vegetable is very tender, so a quick stir-fry is enough.
column9: A spoken word for young and soft things: 嫩葉, 嫩草, tender vegetables, meat cooked just right, baby skin. It is the opposite of 老. It can also mean a light shade of color, or inexperienced when said of a person.

column3: Smooth to the touch and slightly shiny, with no bumps: 光滑的皮肤, 光滑的桌面, a pebble worn by water. The opposite is 粗糙. It describes surfaces only, never smooth talk or a smooth ride. One old explanation of 光 is fire over a person's head, showing light shining out.
column4: 鹅卵石被水冲得很光滑。
column5: 鵝卵石被水沖得很光滑。
column6: Éluǎnshí bèi shuǐ chōng de hěn guānghuá.
column7: The pebbles have been worn very smooth by the water.
column9: Smooth to the touch and slightly shiny, with no bumps: 光滑的皮膚, 光滑的桌面, a pebble worn by water. The opposite is 粗糙. It describes surfaces only, never smooth talk or a smooth ride. One old explanation of 光 is fire over a person's head, showing light shining out.

column3: Rough in texture or in workmanship: 粗糙的手 are rough hands, and 做工粗糙 is shoddy work. It is the opposite of 光滑 for surfaces and of 精致 for craftsmanship.
column4: 冬天我的手变得很粗糙。
column5: 冬天我的手變得很粗糙。
column6: Dōngtiān wǒ de shǒu biàn de hěn cūcāo.
column7: My hands get very rough in winter.
column9: Rough in texture or in workmanship: 粗糙的手 are rough hands, and 做工粗糙 is shoddy work. It is the opposite of 光滑 for surfaces and of 精緻 for craftsmanship.

column3: A tall, grand building, mostly met in the names of office towers and hotels (国际大厦, 帝国大厦). In plain speech a tall building is 大楼. In Taiwan the second character is read xià, so you hear dàxià. In 厦 the part 夏 also adds meaning, because it stands for "great".
column4: 这座大厦有五十层，从上面可以看得很远。
column5: 這座大廈有五十層，從上面可以看得很遠。
column6: Zhè zuò dàshà yǒu wǔshí céng, cóng shàngmiàn kěyǐ kàn de hěn yuǎn.
column7: This tower has fifty floors, and you can see far from the top.
column9: A tall, grand building, mostly met in the names of office towers and hotels (國際大廈, 帝國大廈). In plain speech a tall building is 大樓. In Taiwan the second character is read xià, so you hear dàxià. In 廈 the part 夏 also adds meaning, because it stands for "great".

column3: The narrow lanes of old Beijing and other northern cities, lined with courtyard houses; 逛胡同 is a favorite way to see the old city. Other regions have their own words, such as 巷 or 弄.
column4: 我们在北京的胡同里走了一下午。
column5: 我們在北京的胡同裡走了一下午。
column6: Wǒmen zài Běijīng de hútòng lǐ zǒu le yī xiàwǔ.
column7: We walked around the hutongs of Beijing all afternoon.
column9: The narrow lanes of old Beijing and other northern cities, lined with courtyard houses; 逛胡同 is a favorite way to see the old city. Other regions have their own words, such as 巷 or 弄.

column3: To turn at a corner, on foot or in a vehicle; it takes a measure word in between (拐个弯) and gives directions such as 往左拐. Figuratively 拐弯抹角 is to talk in a roundabout way.
column4: 到前面的路口拐弯，再走五分钟就到了。
column5: 到前面的路口拐彎，再走五分鐘就到了。
column6: Dào qiánmiàn de lùkǒu guǎiwān, zài zǒu wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
column7: Turn at the next intersection and it is five more minutes on foot.
column9: To turn at a corner, on foot or in a vehicle; it takes a measure word in between (拐個彎) and gives directions such as 往左拐. Figuratively 拐彎抹角 is to talk in a roundabout way.

column3: A passenger car of a train or subway, counted with 节 (第五节车厢); it can also be the cargo bed of a truck. The car of a train is not 车, so say 哪节车厢 to ask which car.
column4: 我在第五节车厢，你呢？
column5: 我在第五節車廂，你呢？
column6: Wǒ zài dì wǔ jié chēxiāng, nǐ ne?
column7: I am in car five, and you?
column9: A passenger car of a train or subway, counted with 節 (第五節車廂); it can also be the cargo bed of a truck. The car of a train is not 車, so say 哪節車廂 to ask which car.

column3: Going and coming back, a round trip: 往返票 is a round-trip ticket, and 往返于A和B is to shuttle between the two. It is more formal than 来回, the everyday word for the same thing.
column4: 他每天往返于家和公司之间。
column5: 他每天往返於家和公司之間。
column6: Tā měi tiān wǎngfǎn yú jiā hé gōngsī zhījiān.
column7: Every day he goes back and forth between home and the office.
column9: Going and coming back, a round trip: 往返票 is a round-trip ticket, and 往返於A和B is to shuttle between the two. It is more formal than 來回, the everyday word for the same thing.

column3: A set phrase from travel guides and brochures for sights worth a visit, both scenic spots and historic sites: 参观名胜古迹, 游览名胜古迹. In speech people just say the place name or 景点. The 名 of the first word is said to show saying your own name, 口, in the dark, 夕, to identify yourself.
column4: 北京有很多名胜古迹，比如故宫和长城。
column5: 北京有很多名勝古跡，比如故宮和長城。
column6: Běijīng yǒu hěn duō míngshènggǔjì, bǐrú Gùgōng hé Chángchéng.
column7: Beijing has many famous sights and historic sites, such as the Forbidden City and the Great Wall.
column9: A set phrase from travel guides and brochures for sights worth a visit, both scenic spots and historic sites: 參觀名勝古跡, 遊覽名勝古跡. In speech people just say the place name or 景點. The 名 of the first word is said to show saying your own name, 口, in the dark, 夕, to identify yourself.

column3: To tour a place for pleasure, walking through sights such as a park, a lake or an old town: 游览长城, 游览故宫. It is a bit more formal than 玩 and is used in travel writing and signs. In 游 the right-hand part 斿 hints at travel as well as at the sound.
column4: 我们花了一天时间游览西湖。
column5: 我們花了一天時間遊覽西湖。
column6: Wǒmen huā le yī tiān shíjiān yóulǎn Xīhú.
column7: We spent a day touring West Lake.
column9: To tour a place for pleasure, walking through sights such as a park, a lake or an old town: 遊覽長城, 遊覽故宮. It is a bit more formal than 玩 and is used in travel writing and signs. In 遊 the right-hand part 斿 hints at travel as well as at the sound.

column3: A person of Chinese descent who lives in or holds the citizenship of another country: 华裔美国人, 美籍华裔. A 华侨, by contrast, is a Chinese citizen living abroad.
column4: 他是华裔，但是中文说得很好。
column5: 他是華裔，但是中文說得很好。
column6: Tā shì Huáyì, dànshì Zhōngwén shuō de hěn hǎo.
column7: He is of Chinese descent, but he speaks Chinese very well.
column9: A person of Chinese descent who lives in or holds the citizenship of another country: 華裔美國人, 美籍華裔. A 華僑, by contrast, is a Chinese citizen living abroad.

column3: On the mainland this is October 1 and starts a week-long holiday, one of the busiest travel times; 国庆 alone is the usual short form (国庆假期). In Taiwan National Day is October 10, called 国庆日 or 双十节.
column4: 国庆节放七天假，我们打算去旅游。
column5: 國慶節放七天假，我們打算去旅遊。
column6: Guóqìngjié fàng qī tiān jià, wǒmen dǎsuàn qù lǚyóu.
column7: We get seven days off for National Day and plan to travel.
column9: On the mainland this is October 1 and starts a week-long holiday, one of the busiest travel times; 國慶 alone is the usual short form (國慶假期). In Taiwan National Day is October 10, called 國慶日 or 雙十節.

column3: A summer camp for children or students, run by a school or company and usually built around one theme such as English, science or sports. The verb is 参加: 参加夏令营.
column4: 今年暑假我要参加一个英语夏令营。
column5: 今年暑假我要參加一個英語夏令營。
column6: Jīnnián shǔjià wǒ yào cānjiā yī gè Yīngyǔ xiàlìngyíng.
column7: This summer vacation I will go to an English summer camp.
column9: A summer camp for children or students, run by a school or company and usually built around one theme such as English, science or sports. The verb is 參加: 參加夏令營.

column3: To exchange one currency for another: 兑换人民币, 兑换率 for the exchange rate. It is also used for redeeming points or vouchers for goods, as in 兑换积分.
column4: 我想把美元兑换成人民币。
column5: 我想把美元兌換成人民幣。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ měiyuán duìhuàn chéng rénmínbì.
column7: I want to exchange US dollars into renminbi.
column9: To exchange one currency for another: 兌換人民幣, 兌換率 for the exchange rate. It is also used for redeeming points or vouchers for goods, as in 兌換積分.

column3: Stocks or shares: 买股票, 股票市场. Playing the market is 炒股 (炒股票), and the measure word is 只 on the mainland and 支 in Taiwan.
column4: 他去年买了一些股票，赚了不少钱。
column5: 他去年買了一些股票，賺了不少錢。
column6: Tā qùnián mǎi le yīxiē gǔpiào, zhuàn le bù shǎo qián.
column7: He bought some stocks last year and made quite a lot of money.
column9: Stocks or shares: 買股票, 股票市場. Playing the market is 炒股 (炒股票), and the measure word is 隻 on the mainland and 支 in Taiwan.

column3: An account that holds your money or your records: 银行账户, 开账户, 账户余额. For an online login name the usual word is 账号.
column4: 我在这家银行开了两个账户。
column5: 我在這家銀行開了兩個賬戶。
column6: Wǒ zài zhè jiā yínháng kāi le liǎng gè zhànghù.
column7: I opened two accounts at this bank.
column9: An account that holds your money or your records: 銀行帳戶, 開帳戶, 帳戶餘額. For an online login name the usual word is 帳號.

column3: To pay the bill at a restaurant or shop: 服务员，结账！ It is a verb plus object, so the particles go inside (结了账, 结完账). In bookkeeping it also means to close the books.
column4: 服务员，请结账。
column5: 服務員，請結賬。
column6: Fúwùyuán, qǐng jiézhàng.
column7: Waiter, the check please.
column9: To pay the bill at a restaurant or shop: 服務員，結帳！ It is a verb plus object, so the particles go inside (結了帳, 結完帳). In bookkeeping it also means to close the books.

column3: To haggle: 讨价 is asking a price and 还价 is naming a lower one. It fits markets and small shops, and figuratively any bargaining over terms.
column4: 在小市场买东西，你可以讨价还价。
column5: 在小市場買東西，你可以討價還價。
column6: Zài xiǎo shìchǎng mǎi dōngxi, nǐ kěyǐ tǎojiàhuánjià.
column7: When you shop at a small market, you can bargain.
column9: To haggle: 討價 is asking a price and 還價 is naming a lower one. It fits markets and small shops, and figuratively any bargaining over terms.

column3: To stop something or someone from going past: 拦住 a person, 拦出租车 to flag down a taxi, 拦球 in sports. The thing stopped follows directly, with no 把 needed.
column4: 他在路边拦了一辆出租车。
column5: 他在路邊攔了一輛出租車。
column6: Tā zài lùbiān lán le yī liàng chūzūchē.
column7: He flagged down a taxi at the roadside.
column9: To stop something or someone from going past: 攔住 a person, 攔出租車 to flag down a taxi, 攔球 in sports. The thing stopped follows directly, with no 把 needed.

column3: Doubled or tripled it is laughter, 哈哈 or 哈哈哈, also typed online. Said once, it is an exclamation of triumph or surprise: 哈，我赢了！ The right-hand part of 哈 happens, perhaps by chance, to look like two open mouths.
column4: 哈，我找到了！
column5: 哈，我找到了！
column6: Hā, wǒ zhǎodào le!
column7: Ha, I found it!
column9: Doubled or tripled it is laughter, 哈哈 or 哈哈哈, also typed online. Said once, it is an exclamation of triumph or surprise: 哈，我贏了！ The right-hand part of 哈 happens, perhaps by chance, to look like two open mouths.

column3: A murmur of agreement or acknowledgment, like "mm-hm" or "OK, yes". It is casual, so it fits friends and family more than a formal reply to a superior.
column4: 嗯，我明白了。
column5: 嗯，我明白了。
column6: Èn, wǒ míngbai le.
column7: Mm, I understand.
column9: A murmur of agreement or acknowledgment, like "mm-hm" or "OK, yes". It is casual, so it fits friends and family more than a formal reply to a superior.

column3: A sigh of regret, disappointment or helplessness, usually followed by the complaint: 唉，算了. Said āi, the same character answers a call ("yes?"); this sigh is ài, falling.
column4: 唉，今天又要加班。
column5: 唉，今天又要加班。
column6: Ài, jīntiān yòu yào jiābān.
column7: Sigh, I have to work overtime again today.
column9: A sigh of regret, disappointment or helplessness, usually followed by the complaint: 唉，算了. Said āi, the same character answers a call ("yes?"); this sigh is ài, falling.

column3: To hide yourself so as not to be found or hit, as animals, children and fugitives do: 躲藏起来. Alone, 躲 also means to dodge and 藏 to hide something away.
column4: 孩子们躲藏在树后面，不让妈妈找到。
column5: 孩子們躲藏在樹後面，不讓媽媽找到。
column6: Háizimen duǒcáng zài shù hòumiàn, bù ràng māma zhǎodào.
column7: The children hid behind the tree so that their mother would not find them.
column9: To hide yourself so as not to be found or hit, as animals, children and fugitives do: 躲藏起來. Alone, 躲 also means to dodge and 藏 to hide something away.

column3: The plan of what happens on which day, such as a trip, a conference or a leader's activities: 日程安排, 旅行日程. For a school timetable you say 课程表.
column4: 这次出差的日程已经安排好了。
column5: 這次出差的日程已經安排好了。
column6: Zhè cì chūchāi de rìchéng yǐjīng ānpái hǎo le.
column7: The schedule for this business trip has been arranged.
column9: The plan of what happens on which day, such as a trip, a conference or a leader's activities: 日程安排, 旅行日程. For a school timetable you say 課程表.

column3: The middle ten days of a month, roughly the 11th to the 20th, used in plans, dates and news: 五月中旬. The first ten days are 上旬 and the last ones 下旬.
column4: 我们打算三月中旬去日本。
column5: 我們打算三月中旬去日本。
column6: Wǒmen dǎsuàn sān yuè zhōngxún qù Rìběn.
column7: We plan to go to Japan in the middle of March.
column9: The middle ten days of a month, roughly the 11th to the 20th, used in plans, dates and news: 五月中旬. The first ten days are 上旬 and the last ones 下旬.

column3: In a rush, with too little time to do something properly: 匆匆忙忙 doubles it, and 匆忙离开 is to leave in a hurry. It often explains a mistake, like leaving something behind. 匆 has nothing to do with 勿, despite looking like it.
column4: 他走得太匆忙，把手机忘在家里了。
column5: 他走得太匆忙，把手機忘在家裡了。
column6: Tā zǒu de tài cōngmáng, bǎ shǒujī wàng zài jiā lǐ le.
column7: He left in such a hurry that he forgot his phone at home.
column9: In a rush, with too little time to do something properly: 匆匆忙忙 doubles it, and 匆忙離開 is to leave in a hurry. It often explains a mistake, like leaving something behind. 匆 has nothing to do with 勿, despite looking like it.

column3: Pessimistic: expecting things to turn out badly. Its opposite is 乐观, and it is said of an outlook, as in 对前途很悲观, not of feeling sad.
column4: 他对这次考试很悲观，觉得自己考不好。
column5: 他對這次考試很悲觀，覺得自己考不好。
column6: Tā duì zhè cì kǎoshì hěn bēiguān, juéde zìjǐ kǎo bù hǎo.
column7: He is pessimistic about this exam and thinks he will do badly.
column9: Pessimistic: expecting things to turn out badly. Its opposite is 樂觀, and it is said of an outlook, as in 對前途很悲觀, not of feeling sad.

column3: Flustered and showing it in your movements or voice: 神色慌张, 慌慌张张. It describes how a person looks when composure is lost, while 慌 alone is the feeling (别慌, don't panic).
column4: 他慌张地跑进来，说钱包不见了。
column5: 他慌張地跑進來，說錢包不見了。
column6: Tā huāngzhāng de pǎo jìn lái, shuō qiánbāo bù jiàn le.
column7: He ran in flustered, saying his wallet was gone.
column9: Flustered and showing it in your movements or voice: 神色慌張, 慌慌張張. It describes how a person looks when composure is lost, while 慌 alone is the feeling (別慌, don't panic).

column3: Both "regret" and "a pity", as a noun or adjective: 很遗憾, 留下遗憾. It is also a polite, formal way to deliver bad news, as in 很遗憾地通知您.
column4: 很遗憾，今天的比赛取消了。
column5: 很遺憾，今天的比賽取消了。
column6: Hěn yíhàn, jīntiān de bǐsài qǔxiāo le.
column7: Unfortunately, today's match has been canceled.
column9: Both "regret" and "a pity", as a noun or adjective: 很遺憾, 留下遺憾. It is also a polite, formal way to deliver bad news, as in 很遺憾地通知您.

column3: To be troubled over a problem and not know what to do: 为钱发愁, 发什么愁. It is a verb plus object. 担心 is worrying that something bad will happen, 发愁 is being stuck with a difficulty.
column4: 他为找工作的事发愁。
column5: 他為找工作的事發愁。
column6: Tā wèi zhǎo gōngzuò de shì fāchóu.
column7: He is worried sick about finding a job.
column9: To be troubled over a problem and not know what to do: 為錢發愁, 發什麼愁. It is a verb plus object. 擔心 is worrying that something bad will happen, 發愁 is being stuck with a difficulty.

column3: Watch out, the word on warning signs: 当心台阶, 当心滑倒. It also works as a verb in advice, 当心别感冒, and is about avoiding harm.
column4: 地上很滑，当心！
column5: 地上很滑，當心！
column6: Dì shàng hěn huá, dāngxīn!
column7: The floor is slippery, be careful!
column9: Watch out, the word on warning signs: 當心臺階, 當心滑倒. It also works as a verb in advice, 當心別感冒, and is about avoiding harm.

column3: To shed tears, for sadness, joy or smoke in the eyes. It is a verb plus object, so you get 流了泪 and 流下眼泪, and 流眼泪 is just as common in speech. 泪 is simply water 氵 and an eye 目.
column4: 听到这个好消息，她高兴得流泪了。
column5: 聽到這個好消息，她高興得流淚了。
column6: Tīngdào zhège hǎo xiāoxi, tā gāoxìng de liúlèi le.
column7: When she heard the good news, she wept for joy.
column9: To shed tears, for sadness, joy or smoke in the eyes. It is a verb plus object, so you get 流了淚 and 流下眼淚, and 流眼淚 is just as common in speech.

column3: Hardworking in a disciplined way that is willing to put up with hardship, esp. in study and training: 刻苦学习, 刻苦练习. It is praise, and not used for ordinary tiredness.
column4: 她学习很刻苦，每天都练习写汉字。
column5: 她學習很刻苦，每天都練習寫漢字。
column6: Tā xuéxí hěn kèkǔ, měi tiān dōu liànxí xiě Hànzì.
column7: She studies very hard and practices writing characters every day.
column9: Hardworking in a disciplined way that is willing to put up with hardship, esp. in study and training: 刻苦學習, 刻苦練習. It is praise, and not used for ordinary tiredness.

column3: Frank and open, saying what you think without hiding it: 为人坦率, and 坦率地说 as a way to start, "frankly". It is a compliment about honesty rather than a hint of rudeness.
column4: 我坦率地告诉你，这个计划不太好。
column5: 我坦率地告訴你，這個計畫不太好。
column6: Wǒ tǎnshuài de gàosu nǐ, zhège jìhuà bù tài hǎo.
column7: To be frank, I think this plan is not very good.
column9: Frank and open, saying what you think without hiding it: 為人坦率, and 坦率地說 as a way to start, "frankly". It is a compliment about honesty rather than a hint of rudeness.

column3: Careful and prudent in what you do or say, to avoid risk: 谨慎投资, 态度谨慎. It is more formal than 小心 and fits decisions and statements better than steps on a wet floor.
column4: 投资的时候一定要谨慎。
column5: 投資的時候一定要謹慎。
column6: Tóuzī de shíhou yīdìng yào jǐnshèn.
column7: You must be careful when you invest.
column9: Careful and prudent in what you do or say, to avoid risk: 謹慎投資, 態度謹慎. It is more formal than 小心 and fits decisions and statements better than steps on a wet floor.

column3: Cunning and tricky in a bad way: the fox is the classic 狡猾 animal, and a 狡猾的人 cheats or dodges. It is never a compliment on someone's cleverness.
column4: 那只狐狸非常狡猾，没有人能抓到它。
column5: 那隻狐狸非常狡猾，沒有人能抓到牠。
column6: Nà zhī húli fēicháng jiǎohuá, méiyǒu rén néng zhuādào tā.
column7: That fox is very cunning and nobody can catch it.
column9: Cunning and tricky in a bad way: the fox is the classic 狡猾 animal, and a 狡猾的人 cheats or dodges. It is never a compliment on someone's cleverness.

column3: A teasing or scolding name for a coward, said to friends and children: 你这个胆小鬼. 鬼 is a common ending for people with a bad habit or weakness, as in 酒鬼 (a drunk) and 小气鬼 (a miser); said by a stranger it is rude. 鬼 shows a kneeling figure with an ugly face, which could be a mask.
column4: 别当胆小鬼，试一试吧！
column5: 別當膽小鬼，試一試吧！
column6: Bié dāng dǎnxiǎoguǐ, shì yī shì ba!
column7: Don't be a scaredy-cat, give it a try!
column9: A teasing or scolding name for a coward, said to friends and children: 你這個膽小鬼. 鬼 is a common ending for people with a bad habit or weakness, as in 酒鬼 (a drunk) and 小氣鬼 (a miser); said by a stranger it is rude. 鬼 shows a kneeling figure with an ugly face, which could be a mask.

column3: Unlucky: the everyday word for bad luck or a bad day, as in 真倒霉！ It covers a run of bad luck as well as a single mishap, and 倒大霉 is very unlucky.
column4: 今天真倒霉，一出门就下雨了。
column5: 今天真倒霉，一出門就下雨了。
column6: Jīntiān zhēn dǎoméi, yī chūmén jiù xià yǔ le.
column7: What bad luck today: it started raining the moment I went out.
column9: Unlucky: the everyday word for bad luck or a bad day, as in 真倒霉！ It covers a run of bad luck as well as a single mishap, and 倒大霉 is very unlucky.

column3: To talk nonsense, saying things that are untrue or unfounded. You say 别胡说 or 胡说！ to someone who has said something you reject, and 胡说八道 is the stronger "utter rubbish".
column4: 你别胡说，我什么时候说过这种话？
column5: 你別胡說，我什麼時候說過這種話？
column6: Nǐ bié húshuō, wǒ shénme shíhou shuō guo zhè zhǒng huà?
column7: Don't talk nonsense; when did I ever say that?
column9: To talk nonsense, saying things that are untrue or unfounded. You say 別胡說 or 胡說！ to someone who has said something you reject, and 胡說八道 is the stronger "utter rubbish".

column3: Spoken and typically northern: to put all your strength into it, as in 使劲儿推 or the cheer 再使点儿劲儿！ It is a verb plus object, so 使了很大的劲儿 works. In Taiwan 用力 is the usual word.
column4: 你使劲儿推一下，门就开了。
column5: 你使勁兒推一下，門就開了。
column6: Nǐ shǐjìnr tuī yī xià, mén jiù kāi le.
column7: Push hard and the door will open.
column9: Spoken and typically northern: to put all your strength into it, as in 使勁兒推 or the cheer 再使點兒勁兒！ It is a verb plus object, so 使了很大的勁兒 works. In Taiwan 用力 is the usual word.

column3: To deal with someone or something, to have contact: 和客人打交道, 跟政府打交道. 不好打交道 means hard to deal with, and 打过交道 means to have dealt with them before. 交 began as a picture of a person with crossed legs.
column4: 我的工作要经常和客人打交道。
column5: 我的工作要經常和客人打交道。
column6: Wǒ de gōngzuò yào jīngcháng hé kèrén dǎjiāodào.
column7: My work involves dealing with customers often.
column9: To deal with someone or something, to have contact: 和客人打交道, 跟政府打交道. 不好打交道 means hard to deal with, and 打過交道 means to have dealt with them before. 交 began as a picture of a person with crossed legs.

column3: A polite opener, mainly in northern China, before asking a stranger for a small favor, such as letting you pass or handing you something; it comes first, then the request. In Taiwan people say 不好意思, or 借过 to get past.
column4: 劳驾，请让一下。
column5: 勞駕，請讓一下。
column6: Láojià, qǐng ràng yīxià.
column7: Excuse me, could you let me through?
column9: A polite opener, mainly in northern China, before asking a stranger for a small favor, such as letting you pass or handing you something; it comes first, then the request. In Taiwan people say 不好意思, or 借過 to get past.

column3: It is about voicing disapproval of a person for something they did, so the object is usually a person: 责备孩子. 被责备 is how you say being scolded. 责 has a cowry shell 贝, meaning money, and the idea of a tax or debt.
column4: 老师没有责备他，只是提醒他下次小心。
column5: 老師沒有責備他，只是提醒他下次小心。
column6: Lǎoshī méiyǒu zébèi tā, zhǐshì tíxǐng tā xiàcì xiǎoxīn.
column7: The teacher did not scold him, but only reminded him to be careful next time.
column9: It is about voicing disapproval of a person for something they did, so the object is usually a person: 責備孩子. 被責備 is how you say being scolded. 責 has a cowry shell 貝, meaning money, and the idea of a tax or debt.

column3: Means 'as if', often with 似的 closing the sentence: 他仿佛睡着了似的.
column4: 走进老房子，我仿佛回到了小时候。
column5: 走進老房子，我彷彿回到了小時候。
column6: Zǒu jìn lǎo fángzi, wǒ fǎngfú huí dào le xiǎoshíhou.
column7: Walking into the old house, I felt as if I were back in my childhood.
column9: Means 'as if', often with 似的 closing the sentence: 他仿佛睡著了似的.

column3: With a neutral-tone dao it describes something authentic, such as native-sounding Chinese or true local food. With a full fourth tone it means a tunnel instead.
column4: 她的中文说得很地道。
column5: 她的中文說得很地道。
column6: Tā de zhōngwén shuō de hěn dìdao.
column7: She speaks very authentic Chinese.
column9: With a neutral-tone dao it describes something authentic, such as native-sounding Chinese or true local food. With a full fourth tone it means a tunnel instead.

column3: Used for asking a professional for advice, such as a lawyer, doctor or counselor: 向律师咨询. It is also the name of an advice service, as in 法律咨询.
column4: 我想向律师咨询一下这个问题。
column5: 我想向律師咨詢一下這個問題。
column6: Wǒ xiǎng xiàng lǜshī zīxún yīxià zhège wèntí.
column7: I would like to ask a lawyer about this matter.
column9: Used for asking a professional for advice, such as a lawyer, doctor or counselor: 向律師咨詢. It is also the name of an advice service, as in 法律咨詢.

column3: Declining an offer, gift or invitation politely, often more than once out of courtesy. What is declined follows: 推辞邀请. 推辞不掉 means you cannot get out of it. 辞 probably began with sorting out silk threads, then went to legal pleas, to words, and finally to taking leave and declining.
column4: 他再三推辞，最后还是收下了礼物。
column5: 他再三推辭，最後還是收下了禮物。
column6: Tā zàisān tuīcí, zuìhòu háishi shōu xià le lǐwù.
column7: He declined again and again, but in the end he accepted the gift.
column9: Declining an offer, gift or invitation politely, often more than once out of courtesy. What is declined follows: 推辭邀請. 推辭不掉 means you cannot get out of it. 辭 probably began with sorting out silk threads, then went to legal pleas, to words, and finally to taking leave and declining.

column3: A guest of honor at an event, or a guest on a TV show or panel, spoken of with respect. Someone invited to speak, not an ordinary visitor (客人).
column4: 今天的嘉宾是一位著名的作家。
column5: 今天的嘉賓是一位著名的作家。
column6: Jīntiān de jiābīn shì yī wèi zhùmíng de zuòjiā.
column7: Today's guest is a famous writer.
column9: A guest of honor at an event, or a guest on a TV show or panel, spoken of with respect. Someone invited to speak, not an ordinary visitor (客人).

column3: A second job done alongside a main one or while studying: 做兼职. It works as a noun and as a verb, and its opposite is 全职, full-time. 兼 shows a hand holding two stalks of grain.
column4: 她周末在咖啡店做兼职。
column5: 她週末在咖啡店做兼職。
column6: Tā zhōumò zài kāfēidiàn zuò jiānzhí.
column7: She works part-time at a coffee shop on weekends.
column9: A second job done alongside a main one or while studying: 做兼職. It works as a noun and as a verb, and its opposite is 全職, full-time. 兼 shows a hand holding two stalks of grain.

column3: Children on the mainland learn it first at school, and many people type Chinese on a phone with it; in Taiwan children learn 注音 (bopomofo) instead. 音 is built on 言, with one short stroke added inside its mouth part.
column4: 你会用拼音打字吗？
column5: 你會用拼音打字嗎？
column6: Nǐ huì yòng pīnyīn dǎ zì ma?
column7: Can you type using pinyin?
column9: Children on the mainland learn it first at school, and many people type Chinese on a phone with it; in Taiwan children learn 注音 (bopomofo) instead. 音 is built on 言, with one short stroke added inside its mouth part.

column3: Mostly a noun, as in 标点符号 for punctuation marks, but it is also a verb: 给文章标点. Classical texts had none, so adding it is a task of its own.
column4: 这句话少了一个标点。
column5: 這句話少了一個標點。
column6: Zhè jù huà shǎo le yī gè biāodiǎn.
column7: This sentence is missing a punctuation mark.
column9: Mostly a noun, as in 標點符號 for punctuation marks, but it is also a verb: 給文章標點. Classical texts had none, so adding it is a task of its own.

column3: How you address someone, as a name or title. It is also a verb, and 怎么称呼您? is a polite way to ask what to call a person. 称 has grain 禾 in it, with the idea of measuring grain.
column4: 我应该怎么称呼您？
column5: 我應該怎麼稱呼您？
column6: Wǒ yīnggāi zěnme chēnghu nín?
column7: What should I call you?
column9: How you address someone, as a name or title. It is also a verb, and 怎麼稱呼您? is a polite way to ask what to call a person. 稱 has grain 禾 in it, with the idea of measuring grain.

column3: Leaving words or steps out. 省略号 is the ellipsis (……), and 省略主语 is dropping the subject, which Chinese does very often.
column4: 中文里常常省略主语。
column5: 中文裡常常省略主語。
column6: Zhōngwén lǐ chángcháng shěnglüè zhǔyǔ.
column7: Chinese often leaves out the subject.
column9: Leaving words or steps out. 省略號 is the ellipsis (……), and 省略主語 is dropping the subject, which Chinese does very often.

column3: The characters only copy the sound of 'microphone', so there is no meaning to look for in them.
column4: 请把麦克风递给我。
column5: 請把麥克風遞給我。
column6: Qǐng bǎ màikèfēng dì gěi wǒ.
column7: Please hand me the microphone.
column9: The characters only copy the sound of 'microphone', so there is no meaning to look for in them.

column3: A photo of several people together, and also the act of taking one: 合影留念. It is verb plus object, so the person comes with 和: 和老师合影.
column4: 我们和老师在门口合影。
column5: 我們和老師在門口合影。
column6: Wǒmen hé lǎoshī zài ménkǒu héyǐng.
column7: We took a group photo with the teacher at the door.
column9: A photo of several people together, and also the act of taking one: 合影留念. It is verb plus object, so the person comes with 和: 和老師合影.

column3: Used for deleting files, messages and text on a device. What is deleted follows: 删除文件. 删 on its own is also heard in speech.
column4: 请不要删除这张照片。
column5: 請不要刪除這張照片。
column6: Qǐng bù yào shānchú zhè zhāng zhàopiàn.
column7: Please do not delete this photo.
column9: Used for deleting files, messages and text on a device. What is deleted follows: 刪除文件. 刪 on its own is also heard in speech.

column3: On a computer it is 'paste', after 复制 'copy': 复制粘贴. It also means sticking something on with glue or tape. In Taiwan it is read niántiē. 粘 has rice 米 in it, for glutinous, sticky rice.
column4: 把这句话复制粘贴到这里。
column5: 把這句話複製粘貼到這裡。
column6: Bǎ zhè jù huà fùzhì zhāntiē dào zhèlǐ.
column7: Copy this sentence and paste it here.
column9: On a computer it is 'paste', after 複製 'copy': 複製粘貼. It also means sticking something on with glue or tape. In Taiwan it is read niántiē. 粘 has rice 米 in it, for glutinous, sticky rice.

column3: Browsing the web or looking through pages quickly: 浏览网页. 浏览器 is a web browser.
column4: 我每天早上浏览新闻。
column5: 我每天早上瀏覽新聞。
column6: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang liúlǎn xīnwén.
column7: Every morning I browse the news.
column9: Browsing the web or looking through pages quickly: 瀏覽網頁. 瀏覽器 is a web browser.

column3: Chinese chess, played on a board with a river across the middle. The verb for playing is 下: 下象棋.
column4: 爷爷喜欢下象棋。
column5: 爺爺喜歡下象棋。
column6: Yéye xǐhuan xià xiàngqí.
column7: Grandpa likes to play Chinese chess.
column9: Chinese chess, played on a board with a river across the middle. The verb for playing is 下: 下象棋.

column3: Describes time that is free or a place that is not in use: 空闲时间, 空闲的房间. For a person being free right now, 有空 is the everyday phrase.
column4: 你空闲的时候喜欢做什么？
column5: 你空閒的時候喜歡做什麼？
column6: Nǐ kòngxián de shíhou xǐhuan zuò shénme?
column7: What do you like to do in your free time?
column9: Describes time that is free or a place that is not in use: 空閒時間, 空閒的房間. For a person being free right now, 有空 is the everyday phrase. 閒 shows moonlight 月 peeking through a door 門, for a gap or space.

column3: Almost always in negative sentences: 丝毫不 or 丝毫没有, 'not in the least'. It rarely stands in a positive sentence.
column4: 他丝毫没有发现我在看他。
column5: 他絲毫沒有發現我在看他。
column6: Tā sīháo méiyǒu fāxiàn wǒ zài kàn tā.
column7: He did not notice at all that I was looking at him.
column9: Almost always in negative sentences: 絲毫不 or 絲毫沒有, 'not in the least'. It rarely stands in a positive sentence.

column3: The daughter of a king or emperor. It is also said playfully of a girl who is pampered, as in 公主病.
column4: 从前，国王有一位美丽的公主。
column5: 從前，國王有一位美麗的公主。
column6: Cóngqián, guówáng yǒu yī wèi měilì de gōngzhǔ.
column7: Once upon a time, a king had a beautiful princess.
column9: The daughter of a king or emperor. It is also said playfully of a girl who is pampered, as in 公主病.

column3: The son of a king. In fairy tales 白马王子 is the Prince Charming a girl dreams of. 王 began as a picture of a ritual axe, perhaps of jade, a symbol of the king's power.
column4: 王子和公主结婚了。
column5: 王子和公主結婚了。
column6: Wángzǐ hé gōngzhǔ jiéhūn le.
column7: The prince and the princess got married.
column9: The son of a king. In fairy tales 白馬王子 is the Prince Charming a girl dreams of. 王 began as a picture of a ritual axe, perhaps of jade, a symbol of the king's power.

column3: Power or authority over others, held by a person or an office. A different word, 权利, sounds exactly the same and means a right that someone is entitled to. 权 was first the name of a kind of tree, borrowed for the idea of a standard weight.
column4: 总统的权力是有限的。
column5: 總統的權力是有限的。
column6: Zǒngtǒng de quánlì shì yǒuxiàn de.
column7: The president's power is limited.
column9: Power or authority over others, held by a person or an office. A different word, 權利, sounds exactly the same and means a right that someone is entitled to. 權 was first the name of a kind of tree, borrowed for the idea of a standard weight.

column3: An official license or permit: 驾驶执照 for driving, 营业执照 for running a business.
column4: 开餐馆需要营业执照。
column5: 開餐館需要營業執照。
column6: Kāi cānguǎn xūyào yíngyè zhízhào.
column7: You need a business license to open a restaurant.
column9: An official license or permit: 駕駛執照 for driving, 營業執照 for running a business. 執 joins handcuffs with a hand, for arresting.

column3: To go into business as a career, not a single deal. It sounds a little formal or written.
column4: 他大学毕业后就开始经商。
column5: 他大學畢業後就開始經商。
column6: Tā dàxué bìyè hòu jiù kāishǐ jīngshāng.
column7: He went into business right after graduating from college.
column9: To go into business as a career, not a single deal. It sounds a little formal or written.

column3: Both to put an idea into action and the practice itself: 实践计划, 理论和实践. The saying 实践出真知 says true knowledge comes from practice.
column4: 理论要在实践中检验。
column5: 理論要在實踐中檢驗。
column6: Lǐlùn yào zài shíjiàn zhōng jiǎnyàn.
column7: Theory has to be tested in practice.
column9: Both to put an idea into action and the practice itself: 實踐計劃, 理論和實踐. The saying 實踐出真知 says true knowledge comes from practice.

column3: The basic nature of something beneath the surface: 问题的本质. It turns up mostly in abstract or serious talk. 本 is a tree with an extra stroke on its bottom to stress the roots.
column4: 我们要看到问题的本质。
column5: 我們要看到問題的本質。
column6: Wǒmen yào kàn dào wèntí de běnzhì.
column7: We have to see the essence of the problem.
column9: The basic nature of something beneath the surface: 問題的本質. It turns up mostly in abstract or serious talk. 本 is a tree with an extra stroke on its bottom to stress the roots.

column3: Telling events or facts in order, in speech or writing: 叙述经过. It is neutral to slightly formal.
column4: 请你叙述一下事情的经过。
column5: 請你敘述一下事情的經過。
column6: Qǐng nǐ xùshù yīxià shìqing de jīngguò.
column7: Please tell us how the events went.
column9: Telling events or facts in order, in speech or writing: 敘述經過. It is neutral to slightly formal.

column3: Drawing a general rule from several examples, or sorting points into a summary: 归纳总结. Its counterpart in logic is 演绎.
column4: 请把这些观点归纳成三点。
column5: 請把這些觀點歸納成三點。
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhèxiē guāndiǎn guīnà chéng sān diǎn.
column7: Please sum up these views in three points.
column9: Drawing a general rule from several examples, or sorting points into a summary: 歸納總結. Its counterpart in logic is 演繹.

column3: An outline of the main points of an essay or talk. You make one first: 列提纲 or 写提纲.
column4: 写文章之前，先列一个提纲。
column5: 寫文章之前，先列一個提綱。
column6: Xiě wénzhāng zhīqián, xiān liè yī gè tígāng.
column7: Before writing an essay, make an outline first.
column9: An outline of the main points of an essay or talk. You make one first: 列提綱 or 寫提綱.

column3: Describes goods and places of high quality and high price: 高档酒店, 高档商品. The opposite is 低档.
column4: 这家高档餐厅很贵。
column5: 這家高檔餐廳很貴。
column6: Zhè jiā gāodàng cāntīng hěn guì.
column7: This upscale restaurant is expensive.
column9: Describes goods and places of high quality and high price: 高檔酒店, 高檔商品. The opposite is 低檔.

column3: Luxurious and lavish, said of hotels, cars, weddings and the like. It can also hint at showiness. 华 comes from 華, which began as a picture of a flower and was the original form of 花.
column4: 他们住在一家豪华酒店。
column5: 他們住在一家豪華酒店。
column6: Tāmen zhù zài yī jiā háohuá jiǔdiàn.
column7: They are staying at a luxury hotel.
column9: Luxurious and lavish, said of hotels, cars, weddings and the like. It can also hint at showiness. 華 began as a picture of a flower and was the original form of 花.

column3: In everyday words this reading is only in 便宜, "cheap"; elsewhere 便 is read biàn, as in 方便.
column4: 这件衣服很便宜。
column5: 這件衣服很便宜。
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu hěn pián yi.
column7: This piece of clothing is cheap.
column9: In everyday words this reading is only in 便宜, "cheap"; elsewhere 便 is read biàn, as in 方便.

column3: The style or design of a thing: clothes, furniture, a template. It is usually talked about as new or different: 样式新颖.
column4: 这种衣服的样式很新。
column5: 這種衣服的樣式很新。
column6: Zhè zhǒng yīfu de yàngshì hěn xīn.
column7: The style of this kind of clothing is very new.
column9: The style or design of a thing: clothes, furniture, a template. It is usually talked about as new or different: 樣式新穎.

column3: The center or most important part of something, usually abstract: 核心问题, 核心价值. It is rarely a physical middle.
column4: 这是整个问题的核心。
column5: 這是整個問題的核心。
column6: Zhè shì zhěnggè wèntí de héxīn.
column7: This is the core of the whole problem.
column9: The center or most important part of something, usually abstract: 核心問題, 核心價值. It is rarely a physical middle.

column3: Less important, the opposite of 主要: 次要原因, 次要问题. It sits before a noun or after 比较.
column4: 这个问题比较次要。
column5: 這個問題比較次要。
column6: Zhège wèntí bǐjiào cìyào.
column7: This problem is rather minor.
column9: Less important, the opposite of 主要: 次要原因, 次要問題. It sits before a noun or after 比較.

column3: The ordered steps of a process, such as a recipe or a procedure: 按照步骤. The measure word is 个. 步 shows one foot in front of the other.
column4: 请按照这些步骤操作。
column5: 請按照這些步驟操作。
column6: Qǐng ànzhào zhèxiē bùzhòu cāozuò.
column7: Please follow these steps.
column9: The ordered steps of a process, such as a recipe or a procedure: 按照步驟. The measure word is 個. 步 shows one foot in front of the other.

column3: Even, evenly spread. It describes how something is mixed, divided or spaced: 搅拌均匀, 分布均匀.
column4: 把面粉和水搅拌均匀。
column5: 把麵粉和水攪拌均勻。
column6: Bǎ miànfěn hé shuǐ jiǎobàn jūnyún.
column7: Stir the flour and water until evenly mixed.
column9: Even, evenly spread. It describes how something is mixed, divided or spaced: 攪拌均勻, 分佈均勻.

column3: This reading is for swelling or flushing, as in 脸涨红了 (the face went red). For prices and rivers rising, the reading is zhǎng, as in 涨价.
column4: 他气得脸涨红了。
column5: 他氣得臉漲紅了。
column6: Tā qì de liǎn zhàng hóng le.
column7: His face flushed red with anger.
column9: This reading is for swelling or flushing, as in 臉漲紅了 (the face went red). For prices and rivers rising, the reading is zhǎng, as in 漲價.

column3: The posture or pose of the body: 坐的姿势, 姿势不对. It also covers the form in sports or writing.
column4: 你的写字姿势不太对。
column5: 你的寫字姿勢不太對。
column6: Nǐ de xiě zì zīshì bù tài duì.
column7: Your writing posture is not quite right.
column9: The posture or pose of the body: 坐的姿勢, 姿勢不對. It also covers the form in sports or writing.

column3: To take out and show something to be checked, such as a ticket or ID: 出示证件. It is formal, and the thing shown follows. 出 shows a foot stepping out of a cave, and 示 began as a picture of an altar.
column4: 请出示您的护照。
column5: 請出示您的護照。
column6: Qǐng chūshì nín de hùzhào.
column7: Please show your passport.
column9: To take out and show something to be checked, such as a ticket or ID: 出示證件. It is formal, and the thing shown follows. 出 shows a foot stepping out of a cave, and 示 began as a picture of an altar.

column3: An excuse, usually a flimsy one: 找借口, 以……为借口. It has a negative tone.
column4: 别再找借口了。
column5: 別再找借口了。
column6: Bié zài zhǎo jièkǒu le.
column7: Stop making excuses.
column9: An excuse, usually a flimsy one: 找借口, 以……為借口. It has a negative tone.

column3: Thanks to someone or something that saved you, followed by what happened: 多亏你. It can also be said ironically.
column4: 多亏你帮忙，我才赶上了火车。
column5: 多虧你幫忙，我才趕上了火車。
column6: Duōkuī nǐ bāngmáng, wǒ cái gǎn shàng le huǒchē.
column7: Thanks to your help, I caught the train.
column9: Thanks to someone or something that saved you, followed by what happened: 多虧你. It can also be said ironically.

column3: A miracle, or a result so surprising it seems like one: 创造奇迹. It can describe luck as well as great achievement.
column4: 他从重病中康复，真是一个奇迹。
column5: 他從重病中康復，真是一個奇跡。
column6: Tā cóng zhòngbìng zhōng kāngfù, zhēn shì yī gè qíjì.
column7: His recovery from the serious illness is truly a miracle.
column9: A miracle, or a result so surprising it seems like one: 創造奇跡. It can describe luck as well as great achievement.

column3: To take a risk or do something dangerous: 冒险去救人. As a noun it is an adventure, as in 冒险故事.
column4: 他冒险救出了落水的孩子。
column5: 他冒險救出了落水的孩子。
column6: Tā màoxiǎn jiù chū le luò shuǐ de háizi.
column7: He risked his life to rescue the child who fell into the water.
column9: To take a risk or do something dangerous: 冒險去救人. As a noun it is an adventure, as in 冒險故事.

column3: Describes a task or mission that is hard and heavy: 艰巨的任务. It goes with big jobs, not small chores.
column4: 这是一项艰巨的任务。
column5: 這是一項艱巨的任務。
column6: Zhè shì yī xiàng jiānjù de rènwu.
column7: This is a formidable task.
column9: Describes a task or mission that is hard and heavy: 艱巨的任務. It goes with big jobs, not small chores.

column3: To get in the way of someone or something: 妨碍交通, 妨碍别人. It takes an object.
column4: 请不要妨碍别人工作。
column5: 請不要妨礙別人工作。
column6: Qǐng bù yào fáng'ài biérén gōngzuò.
column7: Please do not get in other people's way at work.
column9: To get in the way of someone or something: 妨礙交通, 妨礙別人. It takes an object.

column3: To suppose. It opens a hypothetical, often as 假设……的话, and is also the noun for a hypothesis. 假 covers both 'to borrow' and 'false'.
column4: 假设你有一百万，你会做什么？
column5: 假設你有一百萬，你會做什麼？
column6: Jiǎshè nǐ yǒu yī bǎi wàn, nǐ huì zuò shénme?
column7: Suppose you had a million, what would you do?
column9: To suppose. It opens a hypothetical, often as 假設……的話, and is also the noun for a hypothesis. 假 covers both 'to borrow' and 'false'.
